name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.27.0 (released 2026-08-04, https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/tag/v2.27.0) is the latest release, adding email-based login, hardening the message templating engine against memory abuse, and graduating PostgreSQL support out of experimental status. Recent releases (v2.26.x, v2.25.0) addressed CPU denial-of-service via message templates, added password reset via magic links, configurable date/time formats in the web app, and an abuse ban-feed for fail2ban integration. Internal refactoring is underway in preparation for horizontal clustering of ntfy nodes. Self-hosters should note that cache databases older than v1.10.0 (pre-November 2021) can no longer be migrated automatically.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL 2.0 (client) — dual-licensed; check repository for exact terms
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026, most recently v2.27.0 on 2026-08-04
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — username/password, access tokens, email-based login, per-topic ACLs, and configurable default access policies
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud instance

breaking_excerpts: Message cache databases from ntfy older than v1.10.0 (November 2021) can no longer be migrated; upgrade via an older ntfy version first, or delete the cache database.
X-Email: yes now requires being logged in with a verified primary email address; previously it could be used without email verification enabled.
Access tokens, IDs, and magic-link tokens are now generated with crypto/rand instead of a clock-seeded PRNG, which may affect integrations relying on token predictability.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a versatile notification library supporting 80+ services and is open-source, but it is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server like ntfy.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cross-device notifications and file sharing with a polished UX, but it is a closed-source commercial service with a limited free tier and no self-hosting capability.

alternatives.name: Alertmanager (Prometheus)
alternatives.review: Alertmanager is powerful for routing and grouping infrastructure alerts in a self-hosted setup, but it is tightly coupled to the Prometheus ecosystem and far more complex to configure than ntfy for simple script-based notifications.
